findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'link from docs/README.md' requirement (Approach + AC4) with docs/README.md's actual convention (lines 241-244: ADRs indexed via the adr/ directory link, individual ADRs deliberately not listed) — either justify an exception for 0059 or retarget the link/AC to the adr/ directory index.
evidence: docs/README.md lines 241-244: 'adr/ — Architecture Decision Records. One file per decision, numbered NNNN-<slug>.md ... Browse the directory for the full set rather than expecting them listed here.'
Grep of docs/README.md for 'adr/' and 'ADR' returns only the single directory entry — none of the 58 existing ADRs (0001..0058) is individually linked from docs/README.md.
By contrast every existing ADR relies on the adr/ directory link, so the plan's per-file link premise is not the established convention.
findings.finding: The plan assumes docs/README.md links individual ADRs, but the repo's convention is that docs/README.md links only the adr/ directory and deliberately does NOT list individual ADRs.
findings.location: Approach ('link it from docs/README.md'); Acceptance Criteria AC4 ('docs/README.md links the ADR and the target resolves'); Files (docs/README.md)
scenarios: Author adds a direct link to 0059 in docs/README.md, contradicting the index's stated 'do not list individual ADRs' rule and diverging from all 58 prior ADRs.
AC4's link check ('docs/README.md links the ADR') is treated as satisfiable only by breaking the index convention, or is unsatisfiable as written.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In ADR 0059, cross-reference the established house expand/contract prior art (docs/migrations.md's committed store-compat fail-closed gate and the 352b legacy-mirror contract-half retirement, plus epic 6c9c's `file|ref` cutover) when explaining the write-both/read-max-then-contract protocol and rollback boundaries, so the ADR presents the protocol as an application of that pattern rather than a bespoke design.
evidence: The plan anchors only the committed-on-branch decision to prior art ('epic 6c9c rejected off-branch relocation') but names no prior art for the mixed-version/rollback protocol itself.

docs/migrations.md already codifies the same expand/contract pattern: the committed `.store-compat.json` fail-closed gate ('the expand phase of an expand/contract rollout: teach every binary to read and fail-closed first') and the 352b legacy signature-mirror retirement ('kept a legacy single-slot ... mirror ... as the expand half of an expand/contract. Task 352b ships the contract half').
Epic 6c9c (closed) established the `lock_backend = file | ref` expand/contract cutover and the convention that 'the design + its rollback path are captured in an ADR.'
ABSENCE: because the pattern is well-trodden in-repo, no novelty exists to justify; the only actionable gap is a missing cross-reference for discoverability, not a novel-architecture defect.
findings.finding: The ADR records a mixed-version write-both/read-max-then-contract migration protocol and rollback boundaries, but the plan does not direct the author to anchor that protocol to the established in-repo expand/contract prior art (docs/migrations.md's committed store-compat fail-closed gate and the 352b legacy-mirror contract-half retirement), risking the ADR reading as a bespoke reinvention rather than an application of the documented house pattern.
findings.location: Plan → Required content: 'The mixed-version protocol: write new plus legacy, read chronological max(new, legacy), then stop and scrub legacy only after direct deployment evidence.'
scenarios: A future reader of ADR 0059 who wants to understand why max(new,legacy) and staged contract are required has no pointer to the house pattern they instantiate.
A later reviewer questions whether the mixed-version approach was reinvented vs. reusing the documented store-compat/352b expand-contract convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art / relationship to existing migrations' note to the ADR that links docs/migrations.md (store-compat fail-closed gate; 352b expand/contract retirement) and epic 6c9c, stating that A2's write-both/read-max-then-contract cutover reuses that documented expand/contract pattern.
